content.text:
Reading the structure region by region, from left to right:

1. **Cyclopropyl ether.** A 1-methylcyclopropyl group is attached through an oxygen: CC1(CC1)O.
2. **Indazole.** The oxygen sits at position 5 of a 2H-indazole, which is drawn as N-N(H) with the NH at position 2. The pyrimidine is attached at C3.
3. **Pyrimidine.** The pyrimidin-4-yl carbon is attached to the indazole C3. The ring runs C4, C5(H), C6, N1, C2(H), N3. C6 carries the piperazine nitrogen.
4. **Piperazine.** It is N-linked to the pyrimidine at one nitrogen. The other nitrogen bears a CH2 that connects to C4 of the piperidine.
5. **Piperidine.** C4 carries both the F and the CH2 to the piperazine. The ring nitrogen bears a CH2 that connects to C3 of the azetidine.
6. **Azetidine.** The ring nitrogen is attached to the aryl ring of the isoindoline-1,3-dione.
7. **Isoindoline-dione.** The N-substituent is a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, with no stereochemistry shown.

Indazole SMILES, written in the 2H form drawn: c1(-c2cc(...)ncn2)[nH]nc2ccc(OC3(C)CC3)cc12. Here the C3 carbon is attached to NH, which is attached to N, then to C7a. In the drawing N is at the top, bonded to C7a, and NH is bonded to C3. This matches the tautomer used above.

Assembled SMILES:

CC1(CC1)Oc1ccc2n[nH]c(c2c1)-c1cc(ncn1)N1CCN(CC1)CC1(F)CCN(CC1)CC1CN(C1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

Checking the ring closures: in c1ccc2n[nH]c(c2c1), c1 is the carbon bearing O, followed by c, c, then c2 (C7a) bonded to n, then [nH], then c (C3), then c2 (C3a) closing to C7a, then c1 (C4) closing to the O-bearing carbon, which makes C5. This is correct.

The isoindoline part is c1ccc2C(=O)N(...)C(=O)c2c1, attached at the azetidine N through the first c1. This is fine.

SMILES: CC1(CC1)Oc1ccc2n[nH]c(c2c1)-c1cc(ncn1)N1CCN(CC1)CC1(F)CCN(CC1)CC1CN(C1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1
